newsitem.title: CHILE: Striking Quebrada Blanca union sees deal near.
newsitem.headline: Striking Quebrada Blanca union sees deal near.

text.p: Union spokesmen at Cominco Ltd's Quebrada Blanca copper mine in northern Chile said a wage settlement may be near to end a five-day old strike after marathon talks over the weekend.

After negotiations into the night Friday and again Saturday, the union leadership was due to meet Quebrada Blanca's general manager Jim Drake on Sunday afternoon for what could be a final round of wage talks, a spokesman said.
"I think we're pretty close to an agreement," said Ildefonso Cordera, a spokesman at Quebrada Blanca's union hall in the northern city of Iquique.

"As it stands now, we're still on strike. But it looks like today we might have something in the way of a solution," he said. Union officials on Friday also said the two sides had made progress in narrowing their differences on monthly wage levels.
The mine's 300 unionized workers walked off the job indefinitely Wednesday when their salary contract expired, following weeks of fruitless collective wage talks.
The mine, located on an arid Andean plateau near the Bolivian border and one of the world's highest mines, makes about 75,000 tonnes of copper a year in electron cathodes.
